transcript.user: My wife lives abroad. Can she come and live with me in Switzerland?
transcript.agent:
Whether your wife can join you in Switzerland under family reunification rules depends on your nationality and your residence status in Switzerland. The legal requirements, conditions, and whether an entitlement exists differ significantly for Swiss citizens, EU/EFTA nationals, and third-country nationals holding specific permits (such as a B, C, or L permit).
[asks] What is your nationality, and what type of Swiss residence permit (e.g., B, C, L, or Swiss citizenship) do you currently hold?

transcript.user: I am an Indian citizen and I hold a C permit (settlement permit). I have been living in Zurich for 11 years. My wife is also an Indian citizen. I live in a 3-room flat and do not receive social assistance.
transcript.agent:
Yes, she can. As the holder of a settlement permit (C permit), you have a legal entitlement to bring your foreign spouse to Switzerland to live with you, and she is entitled to receive a residence permit [1].

To exercise this right, the following statutory requirements must be met:
- **Cohabitation:** You must live together in the same household [1].
- **Suitable accommodation:** You must have a dwelling that meets the needs of your household (a 3-room flat for a couple typically fulfills this) [1].
- **No welfare or supplementary benefits:** Neither of you may depend on social assistance, and you must not draw (nor become eligible to draw due to the reunification) annual supplementary benefits under the ELG [1].
- **Language requirement:** Your wife must be able to communicate in the national language spoken at your place of residence (German in Zurich) [1]. However, at the time of issuing the initial permit, proof of enrollment in a language promotion course is sufficient [2].

**Deadlines:**
Your application must be made within the statutory time limit of five years [3]. This five-year period begins upon the grant of your settlement permit or upon the date of your marriage, whichever occurred later [4]. Once this deadline expires, family reunification can only be approved if important family reasons are demonstrated [5].
[cantonal] Family reunification procedures and entry visas are processed by cantonal and local authorities. In the Canton of Zurich, applications are submitted to the Cantonal Migration Office (Migrationsamt des Kantons Zürich) via your local municipal residents' registration office (Personenmeldeamt / Einwohnerkontrolle).
[cites] AIG Art. 43, AIG Art. 43, AIG Art. 47, AIG Art. 47, AIG Art. 47

transcript.user: Does my wife already have to speak German before coming, or what are the exact language requirements?
transcript.agent:
No, your wife does not have to speak German before arriving in Switzerland.

Under federal law, the language rules apply as follows:

- **Initial residence permit:** While spouses are generally required to be able to communicate in the local national language (German in Zurich) [1], proof of enrollment in a language course is legally sufficient for the initial grant of the permit [2]. If she already possesses German skills, she can instead submit a recognized language certificate [3].
- **Required level:** The language promotion course she enrolls in must lead to at least level A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages [4].
- **Permit renewal:** When the permit comes up for renewal, she must prove that she has achieved oral language proficiency of at least level A1 [5].
- **Integration agreement:** The authorities may make the permit conditional on signing an integration agreement if they determine a specific need for integration [6].
[cantonal] In Canton Zurich, the Cantonal Migration Office (Migrationsamt Kanton Zürich) assesses language certificates and course confirmations (such as the fide language passport, Goethe, telc, or ÖSD certificates) when processing the application submitted via the local municipal administration (Einwohnerkontrolle / Personenmeldeamt).

transcript.user: Wie lange ist meine Kündigungsfrist?
transcript.agent:
Die gesetzliche Kündigungsfrist hängt von der Art des Vertrags ab, sofern vertraglich keine andere Frist vereinbart wurde. Bei einem Arbeitsvertrag beträgt die Kündigungsfrist während der Probezeit sieben Tage [1]. Nach der Probezeit kann das Arbeitsverhältnis je auf das Ende eines Monats gekündigt werden: im ersten Dienstjahr mit einer Frist von einem Monat, im zweiten bis neunten Dienstjahr mit zwei Monaten und ab dem zehnten Dienstjahr mit drei Monaten [2]. Durch schriftliche Abrede, Normalarbeitsvertrag oder Gesamtarbeitsvertrag können abweichende Fristen vereinbart werden [3]. Bei einem Mietvertrag können die Parteien unter Einhaltung der gesetzlichen Fristen kündigen, sofern keine längere Frist vereinbart wurde [4]. Für Wohnungen beträgt die Frist drei Monate [5], für Geschäftsräume sechs Monate [6], jeweils auf einen ortsüblichen Termin oder auf das Ende einer dreimonatigen Mietdauer.

transcript.user: Quanto preavviso devo dare per disdire l'affitto?

transcript.user: Do I have to file a tax return in Switzerland?
transcript.agent:
Whether you have to file a tax return in Switzerland depends on your residency, nationality, permit type, and income: 1. **Swiss citizens and permanent residents (C permit)**: Taxpayers residing in Switzerland must submit a tax return when requested by the tax authorities, and even taxpayers who have received neither a personal notice nor a form remain obligated to submit one [1]. Foreign employees married to a Swiss citizen or a C-permit holder are also exempt from withholding tax and file an ordinary return [2]. 2. **Foreign employees without a C permit (e.g., B or L permits)**: If you reside in Switzerland without a permanent residence permit, taxes are generally deducted directly from your employment income at source [3]. 3. **When withholding taxpayers must or may file**: You are required to submit an ordinary tax return (subsequent ordinary assessment) if your gross annual income reaches or exceeds a determined threshold, or if you have income not subject to withholding tax [4]. In addition, individuals taxed at source who do not meet these mandatory criteria may voluntarily apply for a subsequent ordinary assessment [5].
[cantonal] Direct federal and cantonal taxes are assessed and collected by the cantonal tax authority (kantonale Steuerverwaltung / administration fiscale cantonale) of your canton of residence, which sets local deadlines, forms, and filing portals.
[cites] DBG Art. 124, DBG Art. 83, DBG Art. 83, DBG Art. 89, DBG Art. 89a

* **Binding for future years**: Once you make this request, the ordinary assessment procedure remains binding for all subsequent tax years until your withholding tax liability ends [4]. You cannot opt back into pure withholding tax in later years.
* **Settlement**: The tax already withheld from your salary by your employer is credited towards your final tax bill without interest [5].
[cantonal] In the Canton of Geneva, the application for a subsequent ordinary assessment (Demande de taxation ordinaire ultérieure / TOU) must be submitted to the Geneva tax administration (Administration fiscale cantonale - AFC). transcript.user: Mon employeur doit-il me payer mes heures supplémentaires ?
transcript.agent:
En principe oui, mais la loi prévoit des modalités de compensation et autorise des dérogations écrites :

1. **Paiement et majoration par défaut :** Si les heures supplémentaires ne sont pas compensées par du temps libre, votre employeur doit vous les rétribuer en versant le salaire normal majoré d'un quart au moins (25 %) [1].
2. **Compensation par un congé :** L'employeur ne peut pas vous imposer unilatéralement un congé à la place du salaire ; la compensation par un temps de repos équivalent exige votre accord [2].
3. **Clause contraire dans le contrat ou la CCT :** Le versement de la majoration ou le paiement même des heures peut être exclu par une clause d'un accord écrit (votre contrat de travail), d'un contrat-type ou d'une convention collective de travail (CCT) [1]. Il est ainsi légal d'y prévoir que les heures supplémentaires ne sont pas majorées ou qu'elles sont comprises dans un salaire forfaitaire.
4. **Dépassement de la durée maximale légale (travail supplémentaire) :** Si les heures dépassent le plafond légal de la semaine de travail fixé par la loi sur le travail (en principe 45 ou 50 heures), elles constituent du « travail supplémentaire ». L'employeur doit verser un supplément d'au moins 25 % (dès la 61e heure annuelle pour les employés de bureau ou de commerce de détail) [3], sauf compensation par un congé de même durée avec votre accord [4].
[cites] CO Art. 321c, CO Art. 321c, LTr Art. 13, LTr Art. 13

1. **Validité pour les heures supplémentaires contractuelles :** La loi permet de déroger par écrit au versement de la majoration de salaire ou à la rémunération des heures supplémentaires accomplies au-delà du temps de travail convenu [1]. Une mention écrite claire dans votre contrat est donc valable pour ces heures, sauf si une convention collective de travail (CCT) applicable prévoit des règles différentes [1].
2. **Limite du « travail supplémentaire » (plafonds légaux) :** Cette clause ne peut en revanche pas écarter les règles impératives de la loi sur le travail lorsque vous dépassez la durée maximale légale de la semaine de travail (fixée à 45 heures pour le personnel de bureau, technique ou de vente dans les grands magasins [2], et à 50 heures pour les autres travailleurs). Dès ce seuil, les heures relèvent du travail supplémentaire et doivent obligatoirement être indemnisées avec un supplément d'au moins 25 % (dès la 61e heure annuelle pour le personnel de bureau ou de vente) [3].
